I have been farming these 10.1 mu for 35 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land like my own palm. My son works in Handan and sends some money home, but the crops still have to feed us and pay for themselves. I learned everything from my father and from watching what works on the neighbors' fields.

For the winter wheat, I will plant an improved variety — Jimai or something similar from the seed dealer. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu, and this year I want the same or better. I plow the field with rotary tillage before October sowing. For fertilizer, I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, about 100 jin, and then I topdress with urea twice: once when the wheat turns green and again at jointing. All together that is about 48 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. I think of it as two and a half bags of fertilizer per mu, but the dealer told me the numbers. I irrigate four times with the well: after sowing, before winter, at jointing, and at heading. The electric pump costs money, but if I skip one, the yield drops. I spray three times — herbicide once after sowing, then insecticide when the aphids come, and fungicide if the weather turns wet. I expect 500 kg per mu if it does not freeze too hard.

For the summer maize, I will plant hybrid Dengai 605. Everyone around here uses it because the ears are big and full. After the wheat comes off in June, I plant right away without plowing — no-tillage saves three or four days, and the summer season is short. I put about 80 jin of compound fertilizer in the row at planting, which gives about 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. If the plants look yellow after a week, I might spread half a bag of urea, but usually the base fertilizer is enough. I irrigate twice: once right after planting to help it sprout, and once when the leaves are big and the tassels are coming out. I spray three times for weeds and corn borers. I hope for 550 kg per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year. Every jin is real money. But I would rather spend a little more than risk a bad harvest. A bad year means we lose everything; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. If the neighbors are buying extra urea, I buy extra too. I do the work myself with my wife; at harvest I might hire one or two people for a day. That is what I will do this year.

decision.reasoning_summary: I base my decisions on what worked last year and what my neighbors do. I use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I have seen them yield well on nearby fields. Fertilizer is my biggest expense, and I would rather apply a bit too much than risk losing yield, since my son's off-farm income helps but the farm still needs to support two people. I irrigate four times for wheat and twice for maize using my well, and I spray three times per crop for weeds and pests.
